research.approach: Practitioners recover a restaurant rating by fixing the cause and then answering honestly, not by chasing new reviews. They log every complaint by theme and date, line it up against what changed in the kitchen, staffing and menu, fix the most frequent cause first, and reply to each review quickly, acknowledging the problem, saying what changed and moving detail to a private channel. Reviews are asked of guests in a neutral way, never for a reward, because Google can restrict a profile for fake or incentivised engagement and Australian consumer law treats fake or hidden reviews as misleading. Results lag the fix, so they track rating and bookings weekly rather than expecting an instant swing.

steps.name: Set the reply and review rules first
steps.why: Before any reply or review request, the rules are fixed: nothing is offered for a review, genuine negative reviews are not hidden or argued with, and each public reply is approved. Google can restrict a profile for fake or incentivised engagement.

steps.name: Line up ratings, bookings and what changed on one dated timeline
steps.why: The rating fell in two months and bookings fell with it, and the kitchen team changed in August. A weekly timeline of rating, bookings and changes (kitchen, menu, staffing, hours) shows what moved first and rules out unrelated causes.

steps.name: Check the reviews are genuine and the booking figures are comparable
steps.why: Before acting, experts check whether any recent low reviews look fake or unrepresentative and whether the booking report counts the same things before and after. Genuine negative reviews must not be hidden.

steps.name: Group the complaints by theme, date and session
steps.why: Experts review the latest reviews in bulk, log each complaint type and how often it appears, and note the day and session, so the most frequent cause is fixed first.

steps.name: Find the cause in the kitchen and on the floor
steps.why: Slow service often traces to staffing and pacing, and cold food to holding and delivery from the pass. The head chef and owner test these against ticket times, rosters and covers per session, and test whether the new menu adds prep time.

steps.name: Fix the biggest cause first and brief the team
steps.why: Reviews only recover if the cause is fixed. Changes are small, owned by a named person and dated so their effect can be read.

steps.name: Reply to each review quickly, honestly and specifically
steps.why: Replies acknowledge the problem, apologise, say what changed and take detail offline. Google checks replies against its policies and notifies the reviewer, who may update the review.

steps.name: Ask guests for reviews in a neutral way, with no reward
steps.why: A steady, honest request to all guests helps recent reviews reflect the fix. Nothing is offered, and requests are not limited to guests who are likely to be happy.

steps.name: Track rating and bookings weekly against the fix dates
steps.why: Ratings lag the fix. Experts read the weekly rating and bookings against the dated changes and compare like for like before judging.

pitfalls.text: Offering a discount or free item for a review, or for editing or removing a negative review.
Replying defensively, with generic apologies, or promising fixes that have not happened.
Asking only the guests most likely to be happy, which can look like selective review gathering; check Google's current policy before using any such request.
Hiding or deleting genuine negative reviews, or posting fake positive ones.
Expecting the rating to recover straight after a fix, or judging from a few weeks of bookings.

stages.name: Pin down the goal
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into measured targets, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Agree the reply and review rules
stages.goal: Write the rules for every reply and review request: voice, what may be said about the changes made, what may never be offered (nothing in exchange for a review), what to escalate, and who approves each reply.

checks.name: The rules forbid offering anything for a review, for editing a review or for removing a review
Every public reply needs the owner's approval, and sensitive cases are held for the owner
Statements about changes made are limited to what the owner and head chef confirm

stages.name: Gather reviews, bookings and the timeline of changes
stages.goal: Collect reviews, weekly bookings, the change dates and any service timings into one working file and build one weekly timeline of rating, bookings and changes.

checks.name: Every review in the period is captured with date, stars and text, and the rating timeline is rebuilt from review dates
Weekly bookings match the OpenTable report totals, and the 420 and 340 figures are matched or marked reported only
Dates the owner could not give are marked unknown, not guessed

stages.name: Check the reviews are genuine and the booking numbers comparable
stages.goal: Look for signs that some recent low reviews are fake or unrepresentative, and check that the booking report counts the same things before and after the drop and covers all channels. Genuine negative reviews stay.

checks.name: Any suspect review is listed with the reasons, and is reported through Google's process rather than argued with
Booking counts use the same definition and channels before and after, or the gap is stated
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for diagnosis

stages.name: Find what is behind the drop
stages.goal: Group the complaints by theme, date and session, then test the hypotheses against the timeline, including the kitchen change, staffing, the new menu, booked volume and non-review causes. Keep competing explanations and mark what is unknown.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with evidence and real review quotes
Each finding states whether it started before or after the August change
Each main finding names a competing explanation
Themes from few reviews are marked low-confidence

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked fixes for the kitchen, floor and replies, each with the finding behind it, expected effect, effort, who owns it, confidence, risk and how it will be measured.

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card has effect, effort, named owner, confidence, risk and how it will be measured
No card relies on a reward for reviews

stages.name: Owner and head chef choose
stages.goal: The owner and head chef pick card ids. Ask for the reason when the top card is passed over, and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are recorded
A reason is recorded wherever the top card was passed over

stages.name: Plan the kitchen and floor fixes
stages.goal: Write the chosen fixes as dated, owned changes: pass and holding routine, pacing and staffing on busy sessions, menu prep changes if the menu is implicated, a pre-service briefing, and how ticket or table times will be recorded to show the effect.

outputs.name: Service fixes with owners and dates

checks.name: Only chosen fixes are included, each with a named owner and a start date
Each fix says how its effect will be seen (times, complaints per session, rating, bookings)
Changes are staged so their effects can be told apart

stages.optional_when: No kitchen or floor card was chosen.

stages.name: Draft the review replies and a neutral review request
stages.goal: Draft a specific reply to each recent review, hold sensitive cases for the owner, and write a short, even-handed request routine that offers nothing in return. Replies mention a fix only when it has actually started.

checks.name: Each reply names the actual issue raised and is not a template
No reply or request offers anything for a review, an edit or a removal
No reply promises a fix or remedy the owner has not approved
The request routine goes to all guests the same way, not only those likely to be happy

stages.name: Post approved replies, one at a time
stages.goal: Post each approved reply from the business account in the browser, record the date, and start the neutral review request routine only after the owner approves it.

outputs.name: Reply log with dates and exact text posted

checks.name: Each reply was approved by the owner before it was posted
The posted text matches the approved text
Nothing in any posted reply or request offers anything in return

stages.name: Read rating and bookings against the fixes
stages.goal: Each week, compare rating and weekly bookings with the dated fixes, the 400 a week and 4.4 targets, and last year's same weeks if the owner can supply them.

checks.name: Bookings use the same definition and channels as the baseline
Rating changes are read with the delay after each fix in mind, and fix dates are shown
No reply or request offered anything in return
A verdict is given only after the window, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Record which fixes moved reviews and bookings, propose lasting rules (for example a pre-service check) with their scope, and plan the next round.

checks.name: Every fix is closed with a result
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this restaurant, this season or restaurants in general

hypotheses.statement: Slow service and cold food began after the August kitchen team change, as the new team settled in.
hypotheses.test: Date each complaint and compare with the change date; compare ticket or pass times before and after if recorded.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Complaints about speed or temperature are rare before the change and frequent after it, and timings worsened.
hypotheses.refute_if: The same complaints existed before the change, or the rise started well before or after it.

hypotheses.statement: Floor or kitchen staffing on the busiest sessions is too thin for 70 seats.
hypotheses.test: Complaints by day and session against rosters and covers for the same sessions.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Complaints cluster on sessions with the lowest staff per cover.
hypotheses.refute_if: Complaints are spread evenly or sit on well-staffed sessions.

hypotheses.statement: The new menu, if it changed, adds prep or holding time or disappoints guests.
hypotheses.test: Find the menu change date, and compare dish-specific complaints and speed complaints before and after it.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Complaints name new dishes, or speed worsened when the menu changed rather than when the team did.
hypotheses.refute_if: Complaints do not mention new dishes and timing matches the team change only, or the menu did not change.

hypotheses.statement: Slow service is caused by too many covers booked into peak sessions.
hypotheses.test: Covers per session against complaints and, if available, table turn times.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Complaints rise with covers per session, especially above the level the team handled before.
hypotheses.refute_if: Complaints occur on quiet sessions too.

hypotheses.statement: The rating drop explains most of the booking fall, rather than season, competitors or booking-channel changes.
hypotheses.test: Weekly bookings by channel against the rating timeline, and the same weeks last year if available.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Bookings fell after the rating fell, on the same channels that show the rating, and last year's weeks were steady.
hypotheses.refute_if: Bookings fell before the rating, fell on channels that do not show ratings, or the same weeks dropped last year.

hypotheses.statement: Some of the 18 low reviews are not genuine or come from a single bad night.
hypotheses.test: Check dates for clusters, reviewer history, and details that do not match the restaurant.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Several reviews cluster on one date or show clear signs of being fake.
hypotheses.refute_if: Reviews are spread over dates and look like real guests.

measurement.window: Weekly for the three months; judge a fix only after at least four weeks of bookings and reviews following it.
measurement.min_volume: Read bookings as four-week averages; read rating changes only with a meaningful number of new reviews since the fix, agreed with the owner before the first read.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop and rethink a fix if complaints about the same issue keep rising after it has been in place for the agreed time; stop any practice that offers something in return for reviews at once.
